record.one_liner: Zendesk is a customer service platform covering ticketing, help center, messaging, voice, chat and sales CRM, with APIs for each.
record.auth_notes: Per the Zendesk security-and-auth page: OAuth access tokens are sent as Bearer. Global OAuth tokens are required if distributing an app to multiple Zendesk customers. API tokens use Basic auth as {email}/token:{api_token}; the page labels this method deprecated and recommends migrating to OAuth. End-user email/password works on closed instances only, and anonymous access on open instances only. A third-party report (Workato) says new Basic auth connections were blocked from 2026-03-31; I did not verify that on a Zendesk page.
record.access_notes: Zendesk's developer docs offer a free 14-day trial. Sandboxes are an Enterprise-plan feature, found via search only and not fetched from a vendor page. Free sponsored accounts (up to 5 agents, no expiry) are for Marketplace partner developers only and need an application. I found no permanent free developer tier. The fetched pages do not state which plan a standard trial uses, and they do not say outright that a trial includes API access. After the trial, API use needs a paid Zendesk subscription (plan not verified).
record.blocker: There is no permanent free tier, only a 14-day trial, and the API token (Basic) method is deprecated, so a multi-customer toolkit should use OAuth (global OAuth tokens). There is no general-purpose official MCP server that I could verify.
